newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Western aviation giants line up with Russia's best.
newsitem.headline: Western aviation giants line up with Russia's best.

text.p: Major Western plane makers took part in Moscow's international Air Show for the first time on Tuesday, displaying their latest models at the annual Russian industry showcase.
U.S. Boeing Co showed off its new Boeing 737-700 passenger jet and Airbus Industrie brought its 124-seat A-319 jet in a bid to attract Russian customers.
General Electric also had a big stand at the Zhukovsky military air base 25 km (16 miles) from Moscow and a Russian official said its joint venture had extensive production plans.
"Our U.S. partner is optimistic despite economic difficulties in Russia," said Sergei Kiselyov, deputy general director of joint venture Rybinsk-GE Aviation Motors.

Kiselyov said the venture produced aircraft and gas pumping engines with Russian firm Rybinskiye Motory and planned to turn out the first engines for a 26-seat passenger S-80 jet designed by Russia's Sukhoi military design bureau in 1998.
A total of 23 countries took part in the seven-day show, including many firms from the former Soviet Union.
The previous two shows attracted small foreign firms, but international giants have not seen enough potential in the Russian market until now.
Show organisers said they hoped the show would result in new contracts between Russian and Western firms.

Russian president Boris Yeltsin, who opened the show, asked an Airbus Industrie official how his company planned to conquer the Russian market. "We come here not to conquer, but to expand cooperation, by finding new avenues," the official replied.
Both Airbus Industrie and Boeing said they planned to expand cooperation with Russian titanium producers, whose output is used in aircraft construction.

The Russian goverment has bankrolled the show in a bid to demonstrate the potential of the Russian aviation industry, which is struggling with outdated production lines and a crippling shortage of cash for development.
On the eve of the show, a new Russian aircraft due be presented to the public for the first time, crashed at Zhukovsky during a training flight, killing the pilot.
The Beriyev-103 light transport plane belonging to the Taganrog design bureau fell near the runway from an altitude of 100 metres.
